title: Safari Vehicles Explained: Pop-Up Roofs and Window Seats
excerpt: In Tanzania, most safaris use 4x4 vehicles with a pop-up roof. What to look for in a vehicle and why it matters.
body:
On safari, you spend many hours in the vehicle. It is worth knowing what to expect.

## The standard

Most safaris in Tanzania use a modified Toyota Land Cruiser or similar 4x4, with:

- A pop-up roof for standing and photography.
- Window seats for every passenger.
- Charging points.
- A fridge or cool box for drinks.
- Space for luggage.
- Radio contact.

## Open vehicles

In some private concessions and camps, open-sided vehicles are used. In national parks, closed vehicles with a pop-up roof are usual.

## Number of passengers

Usually up to six or seven. On a private safari, you have the vehicle to yourselves.

## Comfort

Roads can be bumpy. See [long drives on safari](/blog/long-drives-on-safari/).
